bet.dominantBottleneck: Generating a strong enough magnetic field to produce large continuous output without needing an external power source. Permanent magnets scale poorly, and externally excited fields require another generator—the key gap is whether self-excitation via residual magnetism can bootstrap to useful levels.
liveRoutesRanked: feed part of a generator's own output back through its field winding and test whether residual magnetism bootstraps useful output
use a separate battery/generator to excite field magnets
build much larger permanent magnets
defer large generation until better magnetic materials appear
bet.nextDiscriminatingTest: Build a small bench generator whose field winding is fed from its own armature output with no external supply, relying solely on residual magnetism in the iron core to start. Measure whether (a) it self-starts from residual magnetism, (b) output builds up and stabilizes to a steady level, and (c) increasing the load causes the terminal voltage to hold or collapse. This single test decides whether the self-excitation route is viable—distinguishing "bootstraps useful output" from "fails to start or is unstable under load"—before any investment in field strength scaling.
requiredComplements: iron core with reliable residual magnetism (retentivity and demagnetization resistance)
commutation/brush arrangement that preserves excitation current path and polarity during startup and load changes
load control to characterize stability vs. collapse of terminal voltage
knowledge of magnetic saturation behavior near operating field strength
mainFailureRisks: residual magnetism too weak or lost to self-excite at all (no bootstrap)
feedback builds but becomes unstable or regenerative—output oscillates or diverges before reaching steady state
commutation/reversal of armature current while under load demagnetizes the field rather than sustaining it
terminal voltage collapses under even modest load because output power barely exceeds field excitation requirement
magnetic saturation limits achievable field strength well below what 'substantially stronger generation' demands

routeDecisions.route: defer large generation until better magnetic materials appear
routeDecisions.reason: Correct only if self-excitation fails the bench test; hold as the alternative path rather than pursue now.

bet.generalizationBoundary: A bench success (self-start and stable self-excited output at small scale) does not guarantee large-scale viability: saturation, losses, and stability all change with machine size, speed, and load. The evidence would establish the operating principle (residual-magnetism self-excitation) as sound, but not yet the achievable peak field strength or economic output. Failure at bench scale would not rule out modified commutation or exciter configurations, but would strongly weaken the core hope.

the mechanism of how rapid carbon removal interacts with impurity partitioning to produce brittle vs usable metal

overlapping catchment mapping linking households to specific wells/sources

routeDecisions.route: pursue sanitation infrastructure while simultaneously designing discriminating water-exposure comparisons
routeDecisions.reason: Dual-track hedges the wrong-mechanism risk: sanitation helps broadly and plausibly while the water comparison generates discriminating evidence; however it requires the costlier, slower path.

The relative contribution of water versus air/decay transmission, which the comparison may not fully separate if covariation is imperfectly measured
Whether usable records of household crowding, drainage, and smell exist to enable proper matching
